AccessRequestListItemResponse.description:
A request in a listing: everything above, plus who asked.

Only the listings carry the names. ``POST /access-requests`` answers the clinician who
just raised the request, where naming them back would be noise, and resolving it would
add a lookup to a write path. Both fields are nullable so a row whose requester can no
longer be resolved still lists, with its ids intact.
AccessRequestListItemResponse.title: AccessRequestListItemResponse

AccessRequestResponse.description:
One access request as both parties see it: what was asked, of whom, and whether it
is still open. What a clinician may actually *read* is never answered here — that is
``enforce``'s job on each read (docs/SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md rule 3).
AccessRequestResponse.title: AccessRequestResponse

AuditAction.description:
The audit action vocabulary of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md §1, verbatim.

``ACCESS_DENIED`` extends that list. The M3 gate requires that "attempted unauthorized
reads are denied AND logged" (.claude/ROADMAP.md) and ``RECORD_VIEWED`` records only
successes, so a refused read had no truthful action to write. Adding it costs nothing:
members are values in a VARCHAR(32) column, so the vocabulary extends without a
migration.

``RECORDS_LISTED`` extends it again, for the same reason and by the same precedent
(ADR-020). A clinician asking which of a patient's records they may read is a real
access event — SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE rule 3 covers "metadata-beyond-existence" — and no
existing member states it truthfully: ``RECORD_VIEWED`` means one document was read and
is paired with a record id, so reusing it would either invent views that never happened
or leave that pairing unfilled. It is the one member whose event has **no** target at
all: its subject is a scope, which ``patient_id`` already carries. See the target-column
note on ``AuditLog``.

``EMERGENCY_ACCESS`` is deliberately absent: break-glass is Phase 2 and needs its own
ADR (.claude/TODO.md parking lot), and an unused member here would imply a capability
that docs/SECURITY.md's no-break-glass invariant denies.
AuditAction.title: AuditAction

AuditEventResponse.description:
One entry in the patient's append-only trail, as its subject sees it.

Carries what the row carries and nothing else — no clinician or hospital name, because
``AuditLog`` stores neither and this module may not query the tables that do. The actor
is the opaque user id recorded at the time, alongside the role they *then* held: roles
change, and the trail must show the authority someone acted under, not today's.

Three fields are deliberately absent. ``patientId`` is the caller, constant for every
row in the listing and never part of this API's public vocabulary (a patient is public
as their Health ID). ``requestContext`` is the ``X-Request-Id`` correlation key, which
is client-supplied diagnostics rather than a fact about the patient's care. ``createdAt``
is the row's storage instant, which exists to be compared with ``occurredAt`` during a
tamper investigation, not to be shown twice in a timeline.

Exactly one target is set per action — a record for a read, a category for a consent
decision, a request for one being raised — so all three are nullable. The category is
given as its code, never its internal id: that is the vocabulary the whole API speaks.

``eventHash`` is the tamper-evidence digest ADR-004 anchors on-chain (hashes only, never
identifiers or PHI), published here so the owner of the trail can verify it. The digest
algorithm changes to keccak256 at M6 (ADR-019), so it identifies an event's *content*,
not the event: do not treat it as a stable key.
AuditEventResponse.title: AuditEventResponse

CategorySelectionRequest.description: The categories a patient is answering for, shared by approve and reject.
CategorySelectionRequest.title: CategorySelectionRequest

ConsentDecisionResponse.description:
One immutable per-category answer. ``decidedAt`` is the row's creation instant —
for an append-only record they are the same moment by design.
ConsentDecisionResponse.title: ConsentDecisionResponse

ConsentDecisionStatus.description:
The patient's answer for one category. Two members only, by design: a decision is
an immutable historical fact, so there is no pending state to occupy and no revoked
state to transition into — revocation is recorded on the derived ``ConsentGrant`` plus
a new audit event (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md §1).
ConsentDecisionStatus.title: ConsentDecisionStatus

ConsentGrantListItemResponse.description:
A grant in the patient's own listing: everything above, plus how it stands right now.

``status`` is derived by the service from ``revokedAt`` and ``expiresAt`` at the moment
the page is built, using the same predicate enforcement applies — so a client never has
to decide from its own clock whether a grant would still be honoured. The field is named
for the wire convention the other listings follow, but it is a reading rather than a
stored column (``ConsentGrantState`` says so in the domain).

Only the listing carries it. The single-grant responses answer a change the caller has
just made, where the resulting state is not in question, and leaving their shape alone
keeps this addition free of breaking changes.
ConsentGrantListItemResponse.title: ConsentGrantListItemResponse

ConsentGrantResponse.description:
An active permission derived from an approval. ``revokedAt`` is null while the
grant stands; once set, the next read is refused immediately.
ConsentGrantResponse.title: ConsentGrantResponse

ConsentGrantState.description:
Whether a grant still permits a read, and if not, why not.

**Derived, never stored.** ``ConsentRequestStatus`` and ``ConsentDecisionStatus`` are
columns; this is a reading of the two columns enforcement itself consults, taken at a
given instant. There is no state transition to EXPIRED — a grant simply stops being
active when its deadline passes, which is why nothing writes this value anywhere.
ConsentGrantState.title: ConsentGrantState

ConsentRequestStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a clinician's petition (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md §1).

``DECIDED`` means the patient answered every requested category — approving some and
rejecting others is still a decided request. ``EXPIRED`` is reached by the sweep when
``expires_at`` passes with the request still ``PENDING``; ``CANCELLED`` is the
requester withdrawing.
ConsentRequestStatus.title: ConsentRequestStatus

DecisionOutcomeResponse.description:
What one approve or reject call produced. ``grants`` is empty for a rejection, and
``requestStatus`` becomes ``DECIDED`` once every requested category has an answer.
DecisionOutcomeResponse.title: DecisionOutcomeResponse

DoctorProfileResponse.description: A doctor's own profile, with their hospital context.
DoctorProfileResponse.title: DoctorProfileResponse

DoctorResponse.description: A doctor as seen by their hospital admin (and by themselves).
DoctorResponse.title: DoctorResponse

DoctorStatus.description:
Managed by the doctor's hospital admin (ADR-015): self-registration lands PENDING;
only ACTIVE doctors pass the relationship layer for clinical capabilities (M3+).
DoctorStatus.title: DoctorStatus

Gender.description: FHIR administrative-gender vocabulary, SCREAMING_SNAKE per API_GUIDELINES.
Gender.title: Gender

GrantedRecordListResponse.description:
A page of consented records, plus the scope that produced it.

``grantedCategories`` is what makes an empty ``items`` readable: with a live grant it
means the patient holds nothing in what was approved, without one it means nothing was
approved. It also answers a question no other endpoint does — a clinician can see that
a request was ``DECIDED`` but not which categories survived it — so it is the scope, not
a convenience.
GrantedRecordListResponse.title: GrantedRecordListResponse

GrantedRecordResponse.description:
One record as its *grantee* sees it before opening it (ADR-020).

A separate model from ``RecordMetadataResponse``, not a subset of it, and that is the
point: reuse would mean every field ever added for a patient's own view becomes visible
to clinicians with no review step. What a doctor may see here is an allow-list, and
widening it has to be a deliberate edit to this class.

Enough to *choose* a record — which category, when the care happened, who issued it,
whether it came from a hospital or the patient's own locker — and nothing that describes
the document itself. Three fields are withheld on purpose:

- ``originalFilename``: user-supplied text that routinely carries a diagnosis
  ("hiv-panel-positive.pdf"). The upload path already refuses to put it in the storage
  key for exactly this reason (see ``RecordService._store``); a field unsafe to place in
  an object key is unsafe to broadcast across a page. It is disclosed at download time,
  where it is needed and where a single authorized read has already been audited.
- ``description``: free text with no vocabulary, able to say far more about a patient
  than the category the grant was given for.
- ``sizeBytes`` / ``contentType`` / ``processingStatus``: a page-count proxy, an icon,
  and an M5 pipeline state — none of them help a clinician pick a document.

All of them remain available on ``GET /records/{id}``, which authorizes and audits that
disclosure one record at a time. The listing's job is to choose; the read's job is to
disclose.
GrantedRecordResponse.title: GrantedRecordResponse

HospitalAdminProfileResponse.description: A hospital admin's view of their own hospital (registration + GET /hospitals/me).
HospitalAdminProfileResponse.title: HospitalAdminProfileResponse

HospitalAuditEventResponse.description:
One entry in a hospital's own activity log (ADR-023).

A separate model from ``AuditEventResponse``, not a subset of it, and for the same
reason ADR-020 gave: reuse would mean every field ever added for a patient's own view
silently reaching an organisation, with no review step. What a hospital may see here is
an allow-list, and widening it has to be a deliberate edit to this class.

**``patientId`` is absent, and that is the important omission.** The hospital is reading
its own activity, not a roster of the people it touched; the record its staff acted on
is named, and a hospital that uploaded a record already knows whose it is. Publishing a
patient identifier per row would turn an operational log into a patient index.

Also absent: ``requestContext`` (client-supplied diagnostics), ``createdAt`` (the
storage instant, for tamper investigation rather than a timeline), ``eventHash`` and
``hashVersion`` (tamper evidence published to the *subject* of the trail, which a
hospital is not), and every clinical fact — no filename, category display, date of
service, description or file. The action and its target say what happened; nothing here
says what was in the document.

``actorHospitalId`` is not published either: every row in this listing has the same one,
and it is the caller's own.
HospitalAuditEventResponse.title: HospitalAuditEventResponse

PatientLookupResponse.description:
Identity confirmation for a hospital, and deliberately nothing else.

Two fields, both already known to whoever is holding the patient's card: the Health ID
they typed, echoed back in canonical form, and the name to read back to them. Date of
birth, gender, contact details, the internal UUID and every record fact are absent —
the question this answers is "is this the person in front of me", not "who is this
person" (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md §3: hospital admin gets existence + name confirmation
only). Widening it has to be a deliberate edit to this class.
PatientLookupResponse.title: PatientLookupResponse

RecordExistenceResponse.description:
Which categories a patient holds records in — the clinician's discovery view.

Deliberately the *same item shape* as the category vocabulary and nothing more: a code
and a display name. No id, no filename, no hospital, no size, no service date, no
description, and no count — a count is itself clinical signal (three MRIs and thirty
are different stories), so this first cut answers presence only. A distinct response
model rather than a reused one because the two operations mean different things: one
publishes the vocabulary, this one says what a named patient has.
RecordExistenceResponse.title: RecordExistenceResponse

RecordOrigin.description: docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md §1: who brought the record onto the platform.
RecordOrigin.title: RecordOrigin

RecordProcessingStatus.description:
ADR-008 pipeline states. M2 only ever writes UPLOADED — the OCR/embedding worker
that advances records to PROCESSING/INDEXED/FAILED is the M5 AI milestone.
RecordProcessingStatus.title: RecordProcessingStatus

Role.description:
The four platform roles (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md §3, ADR-013).

SYSTEM_ADMIN is a platform-operations role with a hard invariant: it can never
read medical content, so it must never appear in a role gate on a PHI endpoint.
Role.title: Role

SentAccessRequestResponse.description:
A request in the *requester's* own listing: everything above, plus who it is about.

The subject is the one fact a clinician cannot recover from context. A patient reading
their inbox knows every row concerns them; a doctor reading their outgoing list has no
way to tell one patient's request from another's, which makes the listing unusable
without this field. It carries the Health ID — the patient's public business identifier
(ADR-012), and the exact value the clinician typed to raise the request — and nothing
else off the patient row: no name, no date of birth, no internal id.

A separate model from the inbox's item rather than a nullable field on it, so the
patient's response shape does not change and no endpoint gains a field it has no use
for.
SentAccessRequestResponse.title: SentAccessRequestResponse

StaffDisplayResponse.description:
A member of hospital staff as the patient sees them, wherever this API names one.

One shape for requesters, grantees and audit actors, because a patient is asking the
same question in all three places: who is this, and where do they work. It carries no
identifier — the id it was projected from is already on the row beside it — and no
registration number, contact detail or employment status.

``specialty`` is null when the staff row does not carry one, and always for an
administrator; ``hospitalName`` is always present, because staff belong to a hospital
by schema.
StaffDisplayResponse.title: StaffDisplayResponse

post.description:
Ask a patient for access to a set of record categories.

Roles: DOCTOR, and the clinician profile must be ACTIVE at its hospital (ADR-015).
Consent requirement: none — this *asks* for consent, it reads nothing.
Failure modes: 401, 403 (wrong role or inactive clinician), 404 (no clinician profile),
422 (validation, unknown Health ID, unknown category code).

403.description: Not a doctor, or the clinician is not active

get.description:
The patient's consent inbox: requests naming them, newest first.

Roles: PATIENT (own inbox only — the scope comes from the token, never from a
parameter). Consent requirement: none; a request is not record content.
Failure modes: 401, 403, 404 (no patient profile), 422 (bad cursor or limit).

The clinician's own outgoing requests, newest first.

Each row names its subject by Health ID — the identifier the clinician supplied to raise
the request — because a listing of one's own requests is unreadable without knowing who
each one is about. Nothing else off the patient row is exposed.

Roles: DOCTOR (own requests only). A non-ACTIVE clinician may still read this: seeing
what you asked for is not a clinical capability. The response reports status only —
what may actually be read is answered per read by the enforcement check, never by a
listing. Consent requirement: none.
Failure modes: 401, 403, 404 (no clinician profile), 422 (bad cursor or limit).

post.description:
Approve some of the categories an access request asked for.

Each approval is recorded permanently and produces the grant that enforcement reads.
Roles: PATIENT, and only for their own request — another patient's request answers 404,
never 403. Consent requirement: this *is* the consent decision.
Failure modes: 401, 403, 404, 409 (request expired/decided/cancelled, or a category
already answered), 422 (unknown code, or a category this request never asked for).

404.description: No such request for this patient

409.description: Request closed, or category already answered

post.description:
Refuse some of the categories an access request asked for.

A rejection is recorded as permanently as an approval and grants nothing.
Roles/failures: as for approve.

404.description: No such request for this patient

409.description: Request closed, or category already answered

get.description:
The patient's own audit trail, most recent event first.

Every consent decision, revocation and record access concerning this patient, refusals
included — the append-only log is what makes the platform's promise checkable by the
person it is about. Ordered and paginated on the application-assigned event time, which
is also the value the tamper-evidence hash covers.

Roles: PATIENT (own trail only — the scope comes from the token, never a parameter; no
clinician or administrator reads a patient's log through this API). Consent requirement:
none, an audit entry is not record content, and it names no file, date or description.
Reading the trail is not itself an audited event.
Failure modes: 401, 403, 404 (no patient profile), 422 (bad cursor or limit).

Return the caller's authenticated identity.

Roles: any authenticated, provisioned user. Failure modes: 401 (missing/malformed/
invalid/expired token), 403 (unprovisioned account), 503 (provider unavailable).

Every grant ever derived for the patient, newest first, each with its current state.

The patient's own history, revoked and expired grants included: who may read their
records today is only half the question this page answers, and access that has been
withdrawn is a fact its owner is entitled to keep seeing. ``status`` distinguishes the
three cases, read from the server's clock with the predicate enforcement uses, so a
client never has to judge expiry itself.

Roles: PATIENT (own grants only — the scope comes from the token, never a parameter; a
grantee clinician has no listing here, by design). Consent requirement: none, a grant
is not record content. Reading one's own consent state is not an access event, so
nothing is audited — the trail records grants being created and revoked, which is where
a change to who can read anything actually happens.
Failure modes: 401, 403, 404 (no patient profile), 422 (bad cursor or limit).

post.description:
Withdraw a grant. Takes effect for the very next read — no cache, no grace period.

Idempotent: revoking an already-revoked grant returns it unchanged.
Roles: PATIENT, and only their own grant — another patient's answers 404.
Consent requirement: this *is* the consent decision. Failure modes: 401, 403, 404.

404.description: No such grant for this patient

get.description:
The caller's own doctor profile with hospital context.

Roles: DOCTOR. Failure modes: 401, 403, 404 (no doctor profile row).

post.description:
Register the caller as a doctor of a VERIFIED hospital (ADR-015 step 3).

Roles: any *verified* identity — PulseOS claims are not required yet. Idempotent
(repeat calls → 200). The profile starts PENDING until the hospital admin activates
it. Failure modes: 401, 409 (different role / hospital not verified), 422 (validation
or unknown hospital HID), 503 (auth provider down — nothing is persisted).

get.description:
The records one patient's consent currently lets this clinician read, newest first.

Step 4 of the consent flow (docs/SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md) and the step that closes it:
after ``/records/existence`` says a category holds something and the patient approves a
request for it, this is where the clinician learns the record ids. Each item is the
narrow chooser projection of ``GrantedRecordResponse`` — no filename, description, size
or content type; those are disclosed by ``GET /records/{record_id}``, one authorized and
audited read at a time.

``grantedCategories`` reports the scope the page was drawn from, so an empty list under
a live grant is distinguishable from having no grant at all.

Roles: DOCTOR, and the clinician profile must be ACTIVE (ADR-015). Consent requirement:
the page is filtered by the categories consent reports as granted — a filter, never a
verdict. Nothing here permits a read: every record opened from this page still passes
``consent.enforce``, so an id learned here is refused the moment its grant is revoked.
A clinician with no live grant receives an empty page rather than a 403: they already
know this patient exists, having searched the Health ID, so there is no existence left
to protect.

Audited: exactly one event per request — ``RECORDS_LISTED``, or ``ACCESS_DENIED`` when
nothing is in scope. Unlike the single-record reads, this handler *raises* its failures
(ADR-017 does not apply): every ``RecordsError`` below is raised while resolving the
clinician or the patient, which happens before the audit row is written, so no unwind
can discard a trail entry.

Failure modes: 401, 403 (wrong role or inactive clinician), 404 (no clinician profile),
422 (missing/oversized Health ID, unknown Health ID, bad cursor or limit).

The caller's own hospital (ADR-013 layers 1+2 by construction).

Roles: HOSPITAL_ADMIN. Failure modes: 401, 403, 404 (no admin profile row).

This hospital's own activity on the append-only trail, most recent event first.

The organisation's view of the log the patient reads: every upload, read, download and
refusal its staff generated, and every access request its clinicians raised. Ordered and
paginated on the application-assigned event time.

Roles: HOSPITAL_ADMIN. **The scope is the caller's own hospital, derived server-side
from their admin profile — there is no hospital parameter, so no administrator can read
another hospital's activity by changing a query string.** Attribution is the
``actor_hospital_id`` recorded when each event was written (ADR-023), never the actor's
present affiliation, so a clinician who transfers hospitals leaves their history behind.

Discloses the action, when it happened, who did it and which record it concerned — and
deliberately no patient identifier, no tamper-evidence digest and no clinical fact: this
answers "what has my hospital done", not "who are my hospital's patients".

Two absences are expected rather than faults: patient-actor events have no hospital and
never appear here, and events written before migration 0005 carry no attribution, so a
hospital's log begins at that migration. Reading the trail is not itself audited.

Consent requirement: none — an audit entry is not record content.
Failure modes: 401, 403 (wrong role), 404 (no hospital-admin profile), 422 (bad cursor
or limit).

The caller's hospital's doctors, newest first, cursor-paginated.

Roles: HOSPITAL_ADMIN (own hospital only — other hospitals' rosters are invisible).
Failure modes: 401, 403, 404 (no admin profile), 422 (bad cursor/limit).

post.description:
Activate a doctor of the caller's hospital (ADR-015 step 3). Idempotent.

Roles: HOSPITAL_ADMIN. Failure modes: 401, 403, 404 (unknown doctor OR a doctor of
another hospital — indistinguishable by design).

Deactivate (remove) a doctor of the caller's hospital. Idempotent.

The row is kept (DISABLED) — identities referenced by records/audit are never deleted
(docs/DATABASE_DESIGN.md principle 5). Roles/failures: as for activate.

Register a new hospital with the caller as its admin (ADR-015 step 1).

Roles: any *verified* identity — PulseOS claims are not required yet. Idempotent:
repeat calls return the existing hospital with 200. The hospital starts PENDING;
a System Admin must verify it before it can register doctors or upload records.
Failure modes: 401, 409 (registered with a different role), 422, 503 (auth provider
down — nothing is persisted).

Mark a hospital VERIFIED (ADR-015 step 2). Idempotent.

Roles: SYSTEM_ADMIN (platform operations — touches no medical content).
Failure modes: 401, 403, 404 (unknown HID).

get.description:
Confirm which patient a Pulse Health ID identifies, by name.

The safety step in front of ``POST /records``: a hospital files a document against a
Health ID, nothing can move or delete it afterwards, and until this existed an
administrator had no way to check whose history they were about to write to. A valid
Health ID belonging to the wrong patient was therefore an unrecoverable mistake.

Roles: HOSPITAL_ADMIN only. Not DOCTOR — clinicians discover patients through
``GET /records/existence``, which has a different disclosure contract and is left
untouched. Not SYSTEM_ADMIN — platform operations never require patient identity
(docs/SECURITY.md). Not PATIENT — a patient looking up other patients is the
enumeration ADR-012 exists to prevent.

Discloses exactly the Health ID in canonical form and the patient's name, which is the
"existence + name confirmation only" row of the RBAC matrix (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md §3)
and no more: no date of birth, no contact details, no internal id, and nothing medical.
**This confirms an identity; it authorizes nothing.** The upload that follows is
authorized on its own terms by the records module, which still requires a VERIFIED
hospital and re-resolves the Health ID itself.

Consent requirement: none — no record is read, so there is nothing for
``consent.enforce`` to rule on. Nothing here is audited, for the same reason
``/records/existence`` is not: no record was accessed and no truthful ``AuditAction``
member exists. That question is open for both endpoints (.claude/TODO.md).

**Rate limiting: this is a Health-ID oracle and a future rate-limiting surface**, in
the same family as ``POST /access-requests`` and ``GET /records/existence`` (finding
M3-D). It is narrower than either — HOSPITAL_ADMIN only, and a malformed ID is refused
before the database is touched — but it is the first endpoint that returns a *name*,
so it belongs in the same bucket when that lands.

Failure modes: 401, 403 (wrong role), 422 (malformed Health ID, or no patient matches
it — reported distinctly, because ADR-012's check character makes "you typed it wrong"
and "this person is not on PulseOS" genuinely different answers).

Return the caller's own patient profile.

Roles: PATIENT (ADR-013 layer 1 + own-profile relationship by construction).
Failure modes: 401, 403 (wrong role / unprovisioned), 404 (no profile row).

post.description:
Register the authenticated Firebase subject as a patient and issue a Health ID.

Roles: any *verified* identity — PulseOS claims are not required yet (this endpoint
creates them). Idempotent: repeat calls return the existing profile with 200.
Failure modes: 401 (bad token), 409 (registered with a different role),
422 (validation), 503 (auth provider down — nothing is persisted).

get.description:
The record-category controlled vocabulary (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md §1).

Roles: any authenticated user (reference data, no PHI). Failure modes: 401.

The caller's records, newest first, cursor-paginated, optionally by category.

Roles: PATIENT (own records) or HOSPITAL_ADMIN (records their hospital uploaded).
Consent requirement: none — both scopes are ADR-013 layer-2 relationships.
Failure modes: 401, 403, 404 (no profile row), 422 (bad cursor/limit/category).

post.description:
Upload one medical document (multipart) and create its metadata row.

Roles: HOSPITAL_ADMIN (uploads for a patient by Health ID — requires ``patientHealthId``
and a VERIFIED hospital) or PATIENT (uploads to their own locker — ``patientHealthId``
must be absent). Consent requirement: none — uploading creates data, it reads nothing.
Failure modes: 401, 403, 404 (no profile row), 409 (hospital unverified),
413 (too large), 415 (bad type), 422 (validation / unknown Health ID or category /
future date), 503 (storage down — nothing is persisted).

get.description:
Which record categories a patient holds anything in — existence only.

Step 1 of the consent flow (docs/SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md): the clinician learns that
records exist so they can ask for the right categories. The response carries a code and
a display name per category and nothing else — no record id, filename, hospital, date,
description or count — so a caller with no grant learns only what step 1 allows.

Roles: DOCTOR, and the clinician profile must be ACTIVE at its hospital (ADR-015).
Consent requirement: none, and deliberately so — ``consent.enforce`` answers whether a
*record* may be read, which cannot be answered before any grant exists. Every read past
this point still crosses it. Nothing here is audited: no record was accessed.
Failure modes: 401, 403 (wrong role or inactive clinician), 404 (no clinician profile),
422 (missing/oversized Health ID, or no patient with that Health ID).

Metadata of one record the caller is authorized to see.

Roles: PATIENT (own), HOSPITAL_ADMIN (own hospital's upload), DOCTOR (an active consent
grant for the record's category). Consent requirement: enforced for patients and
clinicians at the single choke point; a hospital's own upload is a layer-2 relationship
instead. Every outcome, allowed or refused, is audited. A record the caller may not see
answers 404, never 403 (existence must not leak, API_GUIDELINES).
Failure modes: 401, 403, 404.

post.description:
Issue a short-lived presigned download URL for the record's file.

Roles: as for reading metadata. The URL is issued only after the same authorization
(docs/SECURITY.md), and the event is audited as a download rather than a view.
Failure modes: 401, 403, 404, 503 (storage).

get.description: Liveness probe: the process is up. No dependency checks (that is /ready).
Readiness probe: 200 when every dependency answers, 503 otherwise.
